general-meeting-all-members.what: The one hour everybody attends. Two tracks in the same room — MATLAB on one side, NX on the other. Not a lecture: install, unblock, and put an artifact on the table.
general-meeting-all-members.note: Every session ends with a named thing that exists: a screenshot, a modelled part, a table, a decoded signal.

senior-design-block-a.what: Scope, advisor sign-off, and weekly progress against the signed one-page scope.

ee-senior-design.what: Controls, instrumentation, embedded and CAN scopes.

advisor-sync-dr-wang.what: Siemens licence route, Teamcenter feasibility, NX training material, and instrumentation guidance.
advisor-sync-dr-wang.note: Email sent asking three things: licensing route, whether a university Teamcenter deployment is feasible, and whether Siemens supplies training material.

off-road-targets-read-the-requirement.what: Open STLA Technical Deliverable Requirements Rev 0, section C. Report back the required content, the scoring split, and what we cannot answer yet.
off-road-targets-read-the-requirement.note: Do not summarise from memory. We write each definition of done straight from the submission table.

off-road-targets-battery-and-mass-angle.what: Same section, read for what it demands of the pack: vehicle mass target, tractive capability, and what the battery has to deliver to hit them.

off-road-targets-packaging-and-geometry.what: Same section, read for geometry: ground clearance, approach, breakover and departure angles, suspension travel, tire size, turning radius.

baseline-vehicle-testing-read-the-requir.what: Section J. Report back the test matrix format, the .mf4 data requirement, and what instrumentation has to exist before spring.

pit-requirements-read-all-seven-componen.what: General Deliverable Requirements Rev 2, section B. Seven components: Studio 1, Check-In 1, Micro-Learning 1, Studio 2, Check-In 2, Micro-Learning 2, Open Exploration.
pit-requirements-read-all-seven-componen.note: Several PIT fields are still marked [DRAFT - TBD] in Rev 2. Report which ones so we know what we cannot plan around yet.

read-vdr-rev-0-end-to-end.what: The whole Vehicle Design Rules document. Produce one page of what binds us, with rule identifiers cited so anyone can check it.
read-vdr-rev-0-end-to-end.note: Nine sections are still marked "to be released", several of them safety sections. List those too — scope can still grow.

questions-to-the-organizers.what: Required format: which section, whether it is a clarification or a modification request, our current understanding, and for a modification the language we propose and why.
questions-to-the-organizers.note: Design rules to Nick Moore. Deliverable questions to the organizer named on the dashboard. General questions to Lucas Shoults.

oversee-all-stla-deliverables.what: Standing accountability across every STLA technical submission.

name-all-fourteen-required-roles.what: Eight roles named by the MarCom webpage requirement, plus six named inside technical submissions: CAD Custodian, Off-Road Systems Lead, Battery Systems Lead, Systems Architecture Lead, Vehicle Test Lead, Facilities & Safety Coordinator.
name-all-fourteen-required-roles.note: A missing name is a missing submission. Most of these people already do the work — they need the competition’s title attached.

email-dr-wang-siemens-licence-and-traini.what: Three questions: the correct licensing route for students, whether a university Teamcenter deployment is feasible, and whether Siemens supplies training material.
email-dr-wang-siemens-licence-and-traini.note: If Teamcenter is blocked, that is not a failed deliverable — the requirement explicitly allows a documented alternative process plus an explanation of the primary barriers.

fall-workshop-registration-closes.what: Registration deadline for the Atlanta workshop, 24–26 September.
fall-workshop-registration-closes.note: The dashboard says end of day; an earlier email said 12:00 pm ET. Work to the earlier one.

rev-1-releases-re-baseline.what: Rev 1 of all requirement documents publishes with final dates and point allocations. Read it and circulate a diff, not a rewrite.

team-structure-funded-position-applicati.what: Team structure proposals and funded position applications.

signed-good-faith-agreements.note: The dashboard resolves the earlier conflict: 18 September, not the 7th.

student-leadership-council-applications.what: A student-led advisory council representing the student voice across tracks. No prior experience required.

fall-workshop-atlanta.what: Three days of training, sponsor sessions and the case study panel.
fall-workshop-atlanta.note: The case study is presented by the Student Team Lead, a VSE student and a PIT student. Three specific people who must travel.

case-study-reflection.what: The initial case releases 10 September. An organizer scenario update on 20 September turns selected risks into issues the team must address.

fall-workshop-case-study-reflection.what: Reflection on the case study, submitted after the workshop panel.

subs.l: 6 pages (PDF) or 30 min (MP4) · 50 MB PDF / 1 GB MP4
subs.fn: EIC Y1 - Fall Workshop Case Study Reflection - TEAM Acronym.[pdf|mp4]

fall-workshop-case-study-reflection.note: Presented at the workshop by the Student Team Lead, a VSE student and a PIT student. Only the reflection is scored.

integrated-year-1-workplan.what: Strategic drivers, work breakdown with owners, schedule, top risks and issues, and the university stakeholder plan.

integrated-year-1-workplan-2.what: The team’s current Year 1 baseline, developed with the student leaders who own the work.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 - Integrated Year 1 Workplan - TEAM Acronym.[xlsx|pdf]

integrated-year-1-workplan-2.note: If the workplan is maintained in a system that requires an account or paid access, we must submit a static XLSX or PDF export reviewable without logging in. Reference detailed technical plans rather than duplicating them.

integrated-master-schedule.what: The dependency and date backbone that feeds the Integrated Year 1 Workplan. Anything built here is reused, not duplicated.

university-stakeholder-meeting-preparati.what: Outreach package and value brief for the team’s EcoCAR champion at the university — someone who can influence or enable meaningful support.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 - University Stakeholder Outreach - TEAM Acronym.pdf
EIC Y1 - University Stakeholder Value Brief - TEAM Acronym.pptx

university-stakeholder-meeting-preparati.note: The outreach package must include the actual letter or email sent to the stakeholder plus a one-page public-facing communication plan.

stakeholder-meeting-proof-of-execution.what: Evidence the meeting happened and what came out of it.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 - University Stakeholder Outcomes - TEAM Acronym.pdf

project-status-update-assurance-review.what: A recorded briefing plus the reusable one-page dashboard used in the recording.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 - Project Status Update - TEAM Acronym.mp4
EIC Y1 - Project Status Dashboard - TEAM Acronym.[pptx|xlsx]

project-status-update-assurance-review.note: EcoCAR organizers are the primary audience. A separate presentation deck is not required. Red and Yellow cost nothing when the evidence supports them.

friday-workshops-matlab-track.what: MATLAB Onramp (~2 h) then Simulink Onramp (~3 h), self-paced, browser-based, free through the university licence.
friday-workshops-matlab-track.note: Completion is a screenshot posted in the channel. That is the entire tracking system.

friday-workshops-nx-track.what: Siemens NX student edition. Install, then sketch / extrude / constrain / assemble.
friday-workshops-nx-track.note: The multi-part assembly built here is the asset used in the CAD demonstration video — the training output IS the deliverable asset.

nx-onboarding-documents-materials.what: The material the NX track runs from on Fridays.
nx-onboarding-documents-materials.note: This is the same document as the CAD Management Onboarding Guide, which is 40% of the 15 October submission. Write it once.

senior-design-scope-lock.what: One page per project, signed by three people: the student, the faculty advisor, and the team customer — the sub-team lead who has to consume the output.
senior-design-scope-lock.note: Without the third signature a senior design project drifts away from the vehicle and comes back in April as something nobody can use.

photo-video-and-headshots.what: Team photo at 1024×768 or larger, a horizontal 1080p video of the full team waving and cheering for about ten seconds, and official headshots.
photo-video-and-headshots.note: Headshots must be taken against the same background — a mix of personal photos is explicitly not permitted. Film in the garage or at a recognisable campus location.

fall-workshop-teach-backs.what: Everyone who went to Atlanta gives fifteen minutes.
fall-workshop-teach-backs.note: How eight seats become thirty people’s knowledge. Non-negotiable.

off-road-benchmarking-spreadsheet.what: Benchmark at least three production off-road vehicles across fourteen metrics: suspension architecture, suspension travel, tire and wheel package, ground clearance, approach angle, breakover angle, departure angle, wheelbase, turning radius, differential and driveline architecture, crawl ratio or normalised tractive effort, underbody protection, recovery provisions, other noteworthy features.
off-road-benchmarking-spreadsheet.note: Public specifications are explicitly acceptable and physical testing is not expected. One vehicle per person, one row each, every cell sourced. Best possible first task for a new member — needs no software and no hardware.

off-road-performance-targets.what: Benchmarking, vehicle attribute assessment, and preliminary engineering targets with justification.

freeze-red-team.what: Attacked against the published scoring distribution by someone who did not write it. Comments in writing.
freeze-red-team.note: Team due date = competition due date minus five working days. This window is the fix cycle, not padding.

off-road-performance-target-development.what: Establish quantitative off-road performance targets for the competition vehicle, traceable from benchmarking through to design decisions.
content: Benchmark at least three production vehicles across the fourteen listed metrics
Vehicle attribute assessment: intended customer, operating environments, primary use cases, design priorities, key tradeoffs
Preliminary targets for ground clearance, approach / breakover / departure angles, crawl and gear ratios, tire size, turning radius, vehicle mass, tractive capability, suspension travel
A summary of why the team chose the specific targets
off-road-performance-target-development.role: Designate an Off-Road Systems Lead and identify them in this deliverable.
off-road-performance-target-development.note: These targets feed the VTS template directly, and the VTS feeds every architecture argument that cites it.

three-architecture-matrix.what: Three distinct integrated vehicle architectures, each with its own modeling, integration, battery and feasibility assessment.
three-architecture-matrix.note: At least one must use the Stellantis-provided electric drive unit and at least one a team-sourced unit. Hub motors and P3 positions are prohibited. Manufacturer swaps, software-only changes, gear ratio changes and differential selection do NOT make an architecture unique.

final-technical-report-itec-digest.what: A conference digest on a topic relevant to EcoCAR work, submitted to IEEE ITEC using the conference template.

final-technical-report.what: The ITEC digest plus proof it was submitted to the conference.
content: Follow all ITEC content and formatting requirements and use the conference template
Include a screenshot of the ITEC confirmation email as proof of submission
final-technical-report.note: The ITEC submission track is listed as TBD and the conference deadline may precede this due date. Worth confirming early.

facilities-safety-readiness.what: The Facilities & Safety Binder and a demonstration video.

facilities-safety-readiness-2.what: Facility layout, electrical architecture and operating procedures.
facilities-safety-readiness-2.role: Designate a Facilities & Safety Coordinator responsible for keeping the binder current, and identify them in this deliverable.

integrated-vehicle-architecture-selectio.what: Three unique integrated vehicle architectures with a defended preferred recommendation. The largest deliverable of Year 1.
content: Three unique architectures, each with modeling, integration, battery and feasibility / risk assessments
Clearly identify the preferred architecture and why it beats the two alternatives
Discuss tradeoffs, benefits, risks and implementation challenges
integrated-vehicle-architecture-selectio.role: Designate a Systems Architecture Lead. Must be a member of the VSE swimlane, preferably the VSE Lead.
integrated-vehicle-architecture-selectio.note: Every fall deliverable should be authored as a reusable component of this package. Off-road targets become the VTS justification, the battery workbook becomes the HV design section, the simulation report becomes the modeling assessment. Write nothing twice.

university-it-ticket-teamcenter-nx-licen.what: Open the ticket and get a named IT contact.
university-it-ticket-teamcenter-nx-licen.note: The 15 October deliverable is at risk on an IT constraint rather than an engineering one. If Teamcenter cannot be deployed, the requirement allows a documented alternative process — but we must explain the primary barriers in the demonstration video.

cad-workflow-diagram-8-required-steps.what: One page describing the team’s complete CAD management process.
content: Receiving OEM CAD data
Storing OEM CAD data
Protecting OEM CAD from modification
Creating new CAD parts and assemblies
Managing modified CAD content
Tracking engineering changes
Releasing approved designs
Archiving released vehicle configurations
cad-workflow-diagram-8-required-steps.note: Must identify the CAD Custodian. Teams using Teamcenter identify how it supports each step; teams using an alternative identify the software tools, storage locations, approval process and release management.

cad-onboarding-guide-2-pages.what: Enough information for a new team member to understand and follow the CAD management process.
content: CAD storage locations
User access procedures
File management expectations
Change tracking process
Design release process
CAD Custodian contact information
cad-onboarding-guide-2-pages.note: Write it for a real new member, then have a DIFFERENT new member actually follow it. This is the same document as the NX onboarding material.

cad-demonstration-video-5-min.what: A screen recording demonstrating the process end to end.
content: Teamcenter implementation status
OEM CAD storage location
OEM CAD protection strategy
Working CAD environment
Change tracking process
Release archive location
CAD Custodian responsibilities
cad-demonstration-video-5-min.note: The submission notes permit "either vehicle CAD or a simple CAD assembly with multiple parts" — which is exactly what the NX learners build in weeks two and three. Teams using an alternative to Teamcenter must briefly explain the primary barriers.

freeze-red-team-2.what: Red-team the CAD package on the 22nd, before travel. Comments in writing.

cad-data-management-readiness.what: Our own submission date — three weeks ahead of the competition deadline.
cad-data-management-readiness.note: Why early: it is the only fall deliverable that needs no engineering data, it teaches the submission ritual on a low-stakes item before five deliverables land in five weeks, and it creates the file naming and change-tracking structure every later deliverable lives inside.

cad-data-management-readiness-2.what: An early-year readiness assessment intended to reduce the risk of lost, overwritten, duplicated or improperly controlled engineering data.
cad-data-management-readiness-2.role: Designate a CAD Custodian responsible for maintaining the documented process throughout the competition, and identify them in this deliverable.
cad-data-management-readiness-2.note: The preferred solution is Siemens Teamcenter integrated with NX. A documented alternative process is explicitly permitted where deployment is not feasible.

mass-budget-v1.what: One spreadsheet, a row per added component, an allocated mass, a source for every number, and a named owner per row.
content: Max curb weight is a requirement at 2,154 kg with no tolerance
The Cherokee reference in the same VTS table is 1,972 kg
That leaves roughly 182 kg for the rear drive unit, inverter, team battery, disconnect unit, enclosure, cooling loop, harness and brackets
Almost nothing comes off to pay for it: the stock powertrain, the sealed stock HV battery and the fuel system all stay
mass-budget-v1.note: The VTS footnote defines max curb weight as GVWR minus one 91 kg occupant. Confirm the derivation with organizers, but start from 182 kg rather than waiting.

rear-eaxle-benchmark-packaging.what: Compare candidate drive units on torque, peak and continuous power, speed range, reduction ratio, mass, cooling type and voltage range. Then measure whether one fits under the back of the vehicle.
rear-eaxle-benchmark-packaging.note: Production e-axles and competitor OEM drive units are permitted. Hub motors and P3 positions are prohibited.

baseline-vehicle-testing-characterizatio.what: The measurement plan is written this fall so the spring campaign is not designed in April.
Baseline the donated vehicle so later model-versus-measured comparisons have something to stand on.
baseline-vehicle-testing-characterizatio.role: Designate a Vehicle Test Lead responsible for test coordination, dataset custody, documented procedures and long-term data accessibility.

matlab-simulink-onramp-cohort.what: MATLAB Onramp then Simulink Onramp. Free, browser-based, self-paced, no prior experience assumed.
matlab-simulink-onramp-cohort.note: Completion screenshots posted in the channel. That is the tracking system.

two-controller-compliance-check.what: Confirm our hardware plan against the rule that propulsion controls and HVB controls must be on separate dedicated controllers.
two-controller-compliance-check.note: One paragraph: compliant, or exactly what changes. If any summer plan assumed one box, it changes now.

pcm-onboarding-guide.what: The onboarding guide written for new team members — which is the entire 5 November submission.
content: Introduction to the Propulsion Controls swimlane
Required software, where to download it, installation instructions
Git repo guide
Virtual vehicle model: how to install and run it in Simulink
Software development workflow and version control strategy
pcm-onboarding-guide.note: Finish it three weeks before the deadline, then run the onboarding training FROM it. The training session is the guide being tested by real new members.

onboard-training-runs-from-the-guide.what: Training delivered from the written guide, not instead of it.

pcm-tool-check.what: Submit the PCM onboarding guide plus a schedule of availability for the organizer walkthrough.
pcm-tool-check.note: Include plenty of time slots and the email addresses of everyone who wants to join the virtual walkthrough. Organizers expect a thorough explanation of every bullet in the guide.

organizer-walkthrough-window.what: A live Teams walkthrough with organizers, scheduled from the availability we submit.

virtual-vehicle-simulation-epa-cycles.what: Simulate the provided virtual vehicle model across the three standard EPA drive cycles.
content: A brief overview of each cycle and what it represents — city, highway, aggressive high-speed
Simulated speed trace for each cycle overlaid against the target trace, to confirm cycle tracking
Simulated energy consumption results for each cycle
Discussion of the resulting torque split and control behaviour
Compare our results against published EPA data for the Cherokee and explain the differences

virtual-vehicle-simulation.what: EPA cycle simulation data and a results report.
virtual-vehicle-simulation.note: The content section references a "Video Walkthrough" that does not appear in the submission table. Worth asking organizers whether a video is required. Note also that this deliverable uses a different file naming pattern from the STLA technical set.

nx-cohort-cell-module-modeling.what: Model a cell to datasheet dimensions, array it into a module, then measure the envelope and do the configuration math.

sponsored-cell-specs-module-options.what: External dependency. The 19 November battery workbook cannot start without them.
sponsored-cell-specs-module-options.note: If they have not arrived by early October, escalate that week. This is the single dependency most likely to move a date we do not control.

per-cell-c-rate-check.what: Check peak combined power demand against the rated pulse discharge of candidate cells.
per-cell-c-rate-check.note: The energy chain is the most fragile of the three critical paths. If the C-rate answer lands after the architectures are drawn, that is backwards.

battery-performance-targets.what: HV analysis and the pack configuration analysis that supports the team-built battery design in later years.

battery-performance-target-development.what: The analytical foundation for the team-built battery design in subsequent years.
battery-performance-target-development.role: Designate a Battery Systems Lead responsible for HV analysis, maintaining the configuration analysis, and serving as primary technical contact for battery decisions.
battery-performance-target-development.note: Modules must stay at or below 50 V and the pack is built in 50 V increments. Battery architecture differences alone do not make an architecture unique.

hv-work-permit-battery-build-book.what: A written procedure for every high-voltage activity, plus the build book with PPE callouts.
hv-work-permit-battery-build-book.note: Any hands-on work above 50 V requires a completed NFPA 70E energized electrical work permit, qualified and trained personnel, and the required PPE. Module-level work is low-voltage work because modules stay at or below 50 V.

marcom-manager-named.what: The most exposed unfilled seat on the team.
marcom-manager-named.note: Green Garage Blog 1 is due 8 October on an Absolute deadline and there is nobody in this seat. Communications, Journalism, English or Marketing students get national publication credits out of it.

gate-1-team-program-identity.what: Mission, vision, strategic goals and an About Us section.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 – Team Program Identity – TEAM

gate-1-team-program-identity.note: All contents submitted as a single folder uploaded to Box.

green-garage-blog-1.what: A published story on the official AVTC Green Garage Blog.

subs.f: DOC for blog; JPG or PNG for images
subs.l: 300 word minimum, no maximum · 50 MB per file

content: A minimum of three high-quality, high-resolution team-produced photos
Social media copy for LinkedIn / Facebook and Instagram to promote the story
green-garage-blog-1.note: A blog template is provided on Box and must be used. This is the most urgent MarCom item and the seat is unfilled.

team-webpage-content.what: The official documented team description on file for the whole competition series.
content: About section, 250-word minimum, written in third person
At least one team photo, 1024×768 or larger, including everyone in the program
A horizontal 1080p video of the full team waving and cheering, about 10 seconds, in the garage or at an iconic campus location
Official headshots taken against the same background — a mix of personal photos is not permitted
Names, LinkedIn URLs and professional bios for the lead faculty advisor, PM, MarCom Manager, PIT Lead, VSE Lead, VHI Lead, PCM Lead and HVB Lead
team-webpage-content.note: Categorised as a Team Leadership Requirement rather than a scored deliverable. Eight named roles — a missing name is a missing submission.

gate-2-visual-identity.what: Brand overview, logos, usage standards, palette, typography, visual style and social media style guide.

subs.l: 12 slides excluding title and contents · 50 MB

gate-2-visual-identity.note: Must use the provided EIC PowerPoint template and include PNG logo files separately in the folder.

social-media-video-1.what: A 90-second Reel-style video posted from EcoCAR’s official accounts.

subs.f: Word doc caption; MP4 video; JPG or PNG cover
subs.l: 90 second video · Word 10 MB, MP4 250 MB, image 10 MB

social-media-video-1.note: .MOV files will not be accepted. A caption template is provided on Box.

gate-3-brand-assets.what: A presentation template, report template and letterhead.

subs.l: PPT template 8–10 slides · report template 4–5 pages · letterhead 1–2 pages · 100 MB

gate-3-brand-assets.note: The EcoCAR Communications Team may request revisions after submission.

studio-1-check-in-business-portfolio-rev.what: A per-team 30-minute live review session with organizers and assigned faculty.

subs.f: Link to the team’s draft portfolio workspace
subs.l: no extra slides or documents required
subs.fn: shared link, kept accessible to organizers

studio-1-check-in-business-portfolio-rev.note: Booking links arrive about a month before check-in week. The check-in is dated BEFORE Studio 1 itself — worth confirming with organizers.

gate-4-external-promotion-strategy.what: Audience outreach strategy for in-person and online engagement.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 – External Promotion Strategy – TEAM

gate-4-external-promotion-strategy.note: Developed collaboratively with input from the PM and the technical swimlanes. Four program-set audiences: sponsors, university leadership, prospective students, local K-12.

studio-1-sdv-business-understanding.what: Value chain definition, ecosystem diagram, and the assumptions and hypothesis registry that feeds Studio 2 and eventually Gate 1.

subs.f: Link to the team’s portfolio workspace
subs.l: no extra slides or documents required

studio-1-sdv-business-understanding.note: The portfolio is a living workspace. Keep the shared link accessible to organizers and faculty through the Competition Finale — do not restrict viewing after submitting.

social-media-data-collection.what: LinkedIn followers, posts, impressions and engagement rate tracked from September 2026 to April 2027, plus named Y1 and Y2 admins. Due 7 May 2027 as a Team Leadership Requirement.
social-media-data-collection.note: Start in September or April’s number is a guess. This is irreversible if missed — it cannot be reconstructed later at any price.

outreach-data-collection.what: Event name, date, location, attendee count and audience description for every event. Due 7 May 2027 as a Team Leadership Requirement.
outreach-data-collection.note: Logged the same day. Memory does not survive a week, and every club fair and K-12 visit counts only if someone records it.

pit-customer-discovery-gate-1.what: 8–10 customer discovery interviews, wedge validation, and a Gate 1 recommendation defended live.

subs.fn: EIC Y1 - Gate 1 Recommendation - TEAM Acronym.pdf
EIC Y1 - PIT Y1 Presentation - TEAM Acronym.pptx

pit-customer-discovery-gate-1.note: Whoever presents Gate 1 must have done the interviews themselves. That constraint drives how we split the track with the CBE side.

budget-purchase-log.what: Committed, spent, remaining, by category. Date, requester, vendor, item, amount, status, and where the receipt lives.
budget-purchase-log.note: Anyone should be able to ask "how much do we have left for the battery" and get an answer in under a minute.
